title: Medtrum Pump unreachable after 2 minutes
body:
Medtrum pump + Android 15 + BYODA: I have a problem with Medtrum pump disconnecting from phone and cannot connect back. After phone restart the pump communicates with AAPS about 2 minutes so I can get bolus or set new profile, but after this time AAPS just cannot connect with pump anymore. If I restart the phone, I can control the pump again, but again just for about 2 minutes.

I use:
Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra (Android 15)
BYODA 1.12.1.0 (Dexcom G6)
AAPS 3.3.3.0-dev
Build: 1590206a4a-2025.05.30
Medtrum pump (type MD8201, FW version 1.80.83)

I tried and did not help:
AAPS - Medtrum option - Scan on connection error ON/OFF
AAPS option - BT Watchdog ON/OFF
Uninstalling and clean install of AAPS
Different AAPS builds (3.3.2.0-Tsunami_3.4.1, 3.2.0.4-AutoISF)
Play Protect ON/OFF
New Metrum pump/reservoir

What works?
Setup above, but Danai pump
Setup above, but my older phone (S23+ with Android 14)

Some other users have no problems with AAPS 3.3.3.0-dev + Medtrum + Android 15 combo, but they don't use BYODA (but xDrip for example). So maybe there is some conflict between Medtrum and BYODA on Android 15?

[AndroidAPS_LOG_1748868734664.log.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20572245/AndroidAPS_LOG_1748868734664.log.zip)

As described, I ran the third test today with BYODA/Dexcom G6 BT completely disabled. For this I killed the BYODA app, cleared its cache and removed all "Dexcom *" connections in BT.

After that I switched the pump driver in AAPS from AccuChek/Insight to Medtrum and activated a new patch. All this happened around 14:38 MEST as you can probably see in the logs; AAPS even showed a message that the pump date/time had been updated.

The patch could be activated, but couldn't be used for more than appr. 20 seconds. Trying to update its status on the Medtrum tab in AAPS ran into an endless loop.

I then rebooted the smartphone several times with

(a) nothing changed
(b) BT disabled
(c) BT enabled again

In all these situations the pump connected happily for another appr. 20 seconds. I also tried to emit a mini-bolus of 0.5 units, but it timed out as can be seen in one of the screenshots.

In the Medtrum tab I normally (when no connections appears possible) see as BLE Status the usual bluetooth icon with a black background, while shortly after the reboot this icon is shown with a white background.

FWIW, I ran all tests both with the Medtrum extended setting "Scan on connection error" being on an off, which did not chang

Ok, so after whole day of testing... PROBLEM SOLVED (found)! Medtrum pump communication is somehow in conflict with My BMW app. If you remove "Nearby devices permission" from My BMW app (set it to "Don't allow") the pump works. Dear @jbr7rr do you think that you can fix this conflict somehow? I would like to use My BMW app also. :-)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b80b0322-cca3-4f39-a109-2721dc54e2ae)

Unbelievable! I'll try this myself next, as I found out that communication with an Omnipod DASH pump fails exactly the same way as we have seen with the Medtrum Nano pump/patches!
Thanks for investing your time in trying out everything!

I can confirm that removing "Nearby devices permission" from My BMW app solves the situation for me, too. This is with an Omnipod DASH pod in the meantime, but I think there is a conflict between AAPS and the My BMW app! I'll control the car with my wife's phone now...
@manfred-h thank you too. I hope someone will fix it.

@PetrMlejnek TBH this problem is then with the BMW app and you should report it to them. In our testing with @manfred-h we tried every conceivable hack and workaround but nothing works.

Given that:
- For Manfred the problem also existed with the official medtrum app
- The problem also exist with dash 

I suspect BMW does something dirty/wrong with the Bluetooth API.

So there are two things wrong from my perspective:
- This should simply not be possible in the Android OS, so it should be reported there
- BMW should not do whatever they do and it should also be reported there.

Just had contact with BMW to report the problem with their app. Luckily they cannot claim that this is caused by some other app (ours), because I remembered that I had trouble to connect my smartphone via BT to the BMW charging wallbox last year. Today I tried to connect my wife's phone to the wallbox and failed again; once I disabled the "find local devices in the environment" right for the "My BMW" app, the connection happily succeeded. So, their app conflicts even with their own other app...
Thank you @jbr7rr and @manfred-h for the update, I hope BMW will fix it. Anything I can help with?
